content.title: Guardians vs. Dodgers FREE STREAM today: Where to watch MLB (3/31/26)
content.text: The Cleveland Guardians face two-way phenom Shohei Ohtani and the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers tonight. Find out how to watch for free. (AP Photo/Caroline Brehman)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comLOS ANGELES – After outlasting the back-to-back champs in the series opener, the Cleveland Guardians’ lineup gets a crack at two-way phenom Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers today – Tuesday, March 31 – at Dodger Stadium. This MLB game is available to watch for free on multiple streaming services.How do I watch Guardians baseball for free today?This game will broadcast live on CleGuardians.TV and SportsNet LA at 10:10 p.m. Eastern (7:10 p.m. Pacific). There are two ways to catch this Guardians game free. Fans who have parted ways with their local cable provider can watch at no cost by utilizing a free trial from DIRECTV, which also offers $35 off your first month. FuboTV has a free trial and $25 off your first month. Watch Guardians vs. Dodgers on DIRECTV for freeWatch Guardians vs. Dodgers on FuboTV for freeIs Shohei Ohtani pitching today? Yes, two-time defending NL MVP and two-way sensation Shohei Ohtani is scheduled to make his first start of the season today against the Cleveland Guardians. Best streaming options: FuboTV (free trial and $25 off your first month) and DIRECTV (free trial and $35 off your first month)Here is more information on last night’s victory over the Dodgers from cleveland.com Guardians beat writer Paul Hoynes.LOS ANGELES — During the offseason, the Guardians gave their starting pitchers a message. It went like this: “We ended last season with six starters. We’re going to break camp with five. This is going to be a competition. Be ready.”Rookie left-hander Parker Messick got the message, and he’s pitched like it since the first day of spring training.It earned him a spot in the rotation, and Monday night it earned him a 4-2 victory over the Dodgers, who just happened to win the last two World Series. Messick, in his first start of the season, threw six scoreless innings. He allowed four hits while striking out five. How efficient was Messick? He needed just 76 pitches to go six innings, an average of just under 13 pitches per inning.“What an outstanding outing that was,” said manager Stephen Vogt. “It just felt like he was in control the whole time. He stayed smooth, executed pitches and got quick outs.”Messick said it was an “amazing opportunity” to be able to face a lineup that accounts for a good portion of the Dodgers’ $317 million payroll.“It was one of the coolest things a rookie can ask for,” said Messick. “I’m so grateful I was able to go out there and glorify the Lord.
